prompt: Implement the provided Discountable interface in SeasonalOffer: supply the two abstract methods, clamp the discount into 0..75, override label() using Discountable.super.label(), and delegate bestPrice to the interface's static cheapest method.
explanation: A default method lets an interface ship working behaviour that every implementer inherits, so finalPrice is written once and computed from whatever basePrice and discountPercent the class chooses to report. An overriding class can still reach the version it replaced through InterfaceName.super.method(), which is how label adds a prefix without copying the inherited text. A static interface method belongs to the interface itself rather than to any instance, so it is called as Discountable.cheapest(...) and is never inherited by the class.
hints: Clamp in the constructor, not in the getter: store 0 when the requested percent is below 0 and 75 when it is above 75.
Inside your override, the inherited default is reached as Discountable.super.label() -- plain super.label() would look in Object instead.
A static interface method is not inherited, so bestPrice must name the interface: return Discountable.cheapest(offers);
